chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Murad ibn Kharijah, who said:
Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: As for me, when it is Friday, and the sun is in the east at the same measure as it would be from the west at the time of salat al-'asr, I pray six rak'ahs.
Then when the day has broadened, I pray six rak'ahs.
Then when the sun declines or passes the meridian, I pray two rak'ahs, then I pray al-zuhr, then I pray six after it.

key_terms.بَعْدَهَا: after it, referring to prayer performed after al-zuhr
key_terms.زَاغَتِ ٱلشَّمْسُ: when the sun declines from the meridian
key_terms.صَلَاةِ ٱلْعَصْرِ: salat al-'asr, referenced as a point of comparison for the sun’s position
key_terms.يَوْمُ ٱلْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, the day on which these nawafil are specifically arranged
key_terms.ٱلشَّمْسُ: the sun, used here to mark the prayer timing
key_terms.ٱلظُّهْرَ: the zuhr prayer performed after the preceding two rak'ahs
key_terms.ٱنْتَفَخَ ٱلنَّهَارُ: when the day has broadened or advanced

ai.seo_question: How are the Friday nawafil performed before zawal according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the timing and distribution of recommended nawafil on Friday before and around zawal. It indicates a structured pattern of supererogatory prayer associated with Friday, showing the special devotional character of that day in Shia fiqh.
